text:
I understand you are the mother; please tell me, when did the vomiting first start, and has the baby passed any stool since birth?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction.

speaker: Doctor
text: That X-ray confirms a distal obstruction; did the baby have any prenatal ultrasound findings or a history of polyhydramnios? Also, does the family have a history of congenital anomalies like imperforate anus?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease. The clinical picture of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium in the first 48 hours, abdominal distension, and a distal obstruction on X-ray strongly suggests aganglionosis. We should proceed with a contrast enema and rectal biopsy to confirm the diagnosis.
